adversarialNotesOnThisDesign: The release leans entirely on the source prefix. It is safe here only because no other writer emits that package name on these five rails, and that fact is MEASURED (0 foreign value cells on the rails) AND asserted (the disjoint-rail-sets falsifier). If a future writer composes the same prefix on a setback rail, the release would start moving its cells; the falsifier is what makes that visible.
The version compare is int[] and not a string compare because 1.10.0 versus 1.4.0 inverts. Both sides are asserted on that pair, and leg 1 runs it through Postgres rather than trusting the reading.

Releasing a parcel only when EVERY present rail is movable avoids the partial write, but it also means a single foreign rail freezes the whole set. Measured zero today; counted and named (`staleCorpusBlocked`) so it cannot be silent if it appears.
A re-stamp does move `updated_at` (the UPDATE's SET clause). That is intended -- the citation really did change -- but it means a re-stamp is not invisible to a reader watching updated_at.
